Hot Harley Nights Revs Up For 20th Year Of Generosity

A few years ago, my dad bought me a bike as a gift as he knew I wanted to get back into biking. He got me a Giant Trance x2 which I assumed to be medium sized. I'm 5'10" or 5'11" if it's a good day. So I'm just at the border of medium and large frames. I always found the bike a tad too small, and figured I'd just get a longer seatpost (410mm, and setback). That solved the problem and now I'm all comfy biking around; legs pretty much straight with a very slight bend, no back or hand pains even after a long ride.

One day fiddling with the bike, I find a small sticker with the letter S on it. So it turns out I've been riding a small all along.

Question is: Since I'm now comfortable riding the bike, is there anything else I'm missing which would necessitate a change of frame sizes? From how I understand it, only the toptube and seattube would be different in frame size changes, and the seatpost solved both of those.

I find being able to maneuver better on a smaller frame but loosing stability. If you like going fast you might want to try a larger frame. I also felt like I was going to go over the handle bars more with a smaller frame. So I wasn't as ballsy going down hill as I normally am.
I think the setback in the seatpost helped me with that, I have no feelings of being too much forward or going over the bars. I love going fast but I think this one is fast enough for me for now.
You could also try out different stem lengths if you ever start to feel like its bothering you again. Also, if you have long arms, wider bars can help relieve back pain from a short bike.
